evidence.title: Upholding the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons for World Peace and Development
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.claim: China called for continued strategic-stability communication and in-depth dialogue on reducing the role of nuclear weapons in national security doctrines, including on missile defense, outer space, cyberspace, and artificial intelligence.

evidence.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Zhao Lijian's Regular Press Conference on November 30, 2022
evidence.publisher: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Ireland
evidence.claim: In response to the Pentagon's forecast, Zhao Lijian said China follows a self-defensive nuclear strategy, sticks to no-first-use, exercises utmost restraint, keeps capabilities at the minimum level required by national security, and is never part of any arms race.
evidence.locator: Q&A response to AFP on the Pentagon report

evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect, but directly tied to the Xi-led state's nuclear posture claim.
contrary_evidence: This is self-justification and may understate the pace of modernization.
It does not address the 2022 silo-field buildup.

evidence.title: China nuclear warhead stockpile to reach 1,500 by 2035 if it continues its build-up pace, US says
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the Pentagon said China had more than 400 nuclear warheads in 2021 and could reach about 1,500 by 2035 if the current buildup pace continued, with Xi having signaled at the Party Congress that China would strengthen strategic deterrence.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material; it links the build-up trend to Xi-era strategic deterrence policy.
contrary_evidence: This is a U.S. estimate, not a Chinese disclosure.
It does not by itself prove a doctrinal change away from no-first-use.

evidence.title: Nuclear Notebook: Chinese nuclear weapons, 2023
evidence.publisher: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists / Federation of American Scientists
evidence.claim: FAS estimated that China's stockpile included roughly 410 nuclear warheads, with more in production, and noted that China had significantly advanced construction of its three new missile silo fields for solid-fuel ICBMs.

evidence.period_fit: Good retrospective fit for the 2022 end-state and the buildup underway by late 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important for posture change under Xi's leadership.
contrary_evidence: It is an estimate, not a Chinese official count.
The notebook does not prove intended use or crisis intent.

evidence.title: Arms Control and Proliferation Profile: China
evidence.claim: The profile says China's nuclear policy has been defined by minimum capabilities needed to deter a first strike, while also stating that China is now expanding its force through new silo fields and silos at existing fields.

evidence.title: Full Text: China's Export Controls

evidence.period_fit: Good structural fit for 2022 because the regime was already in force and still operative during the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but materially tied to Xi-era governance of dual-use risk.

It does not cover all AI/cyber/bio choices made in 2022.

evidence.title: China halts high-level military dialogue with U.S., suspends other cooperation
evidence.claim: China halted senior-level military dialogue with the United States and cancelled a maritime military-security meeting after Pelosi's Taiwan visit, a move Reuters said raised the risk of accidental escalation at a critical moment.
evidence.locator: lead and lines 418-420 in the article mirror

evidence.title: Full Text: The Taiwan Question and China's Reunification in the New Era
evidence.claim: The white paper states that peaceful reunification is the first choice and that use of force would be the last resort under compelling circumstances.
evidence.locator: white paper text and the Aug. 17 press conference explanation

evidence.title: Xi Jinping: Put China-U.S. relationship on the right course and bring it back to the track of healthy and stable growth
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.claim: Xi said the Bali meeting should stabilize China-U.S. ties, improve world peace and stability, and put the relationship back on a healthy and steady track.

evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for late-2022 diplomatic crisis management and bilateral de-escalation.

contrary_evidence: This is a diplomatic aspiration, not proof of durable restraint or changed conduct.
The same period still included Taiwan coercion and military signaling.

evidence.title: President Xi Jinping Held Talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.claim: Xi and Putin held extensive talks on international strategic security and said their coordination would help maintain world strategic security and stability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official readout of the Xi-Putin summit and joint line on strategic security.
evidence.period_fit: Strong fit for the inherited strategic posture at the start of 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for Xi's diplomatic choice to deepen strategic coordination with Russia.
contrary_evidence: This is not a peace settlement and it predates Russia's full-scale invasion by weeks.
The language is broad and strategic, not a concrete conflict-de-escalation measure.

evidence.title: Xi talks with Putin over phone
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.claim: Xi said China and Russia would continue supporting each other on core sovereignty and security interests and deepen strategic coordination in the UN and other forums.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct.
contrary_evidence: This supports alignment with Russia more than peace restraint.
It does not show any Chinese effort to distance itself from the invasion of Ukraine.

evidence.title: Wang Yi Expounds China's Five-Point Position on the Current Ukraine Issue
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.claim: China urged restraint, direct Russia-Ukraine dialogue, and support for a peaceful settlement while saying civilians should be protected from a worsening crisis.

That makes it qualified restraint, not principled opposition to aggression.

evidence.title: Wang Yi Attends UN Security Council Foreign Ministers' Meeting on Ukraine Issue
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.claim: China called for renewed dialogue, restraint, civilian protection, safeguards for nuclear facilities, and mediation to promote a political settlement in Ukraine.

It is still declaratory rather than an operational peace action.

evidence.title: Taiwan Work Office of CPC Central Committee issues statement on Pelosi's visit to Taiwan
evidence.claim: The Party's Taiwan office said Pelosi's visit seriously infringed China's sovereignty, violated the one-China principle, and sent a wrong signal to Taiwan independence forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Chinese party-state statement on the trigger for the Taiwan crisis.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct as a statement of the Xi-led party-state position.

evidence.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Hua Chunying’s Regular Press Conference on August 3, 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.claim: China said the Taiwan drills were necessary and legitimate, and that safety alerts and navigation warnings were issued before they began.

contrary_evidence: The same passage says the drills were a way to 'speak' to adversaries, which sounds coercive.
Independent reporting described blockade-like effects and high escalation risk.

evidence.title: China halts high-level military dialogue with U.S., suspends other cooperation

The move reduced crisis communication channels at a tense moment.

evidence.title: Taiwan full of praise, support for Taiwan during visit that infuriated China

evidence.title: China Stays Committed to Peace, Stability and Order in The South China Sea
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

evidence.period_fit: Good fit for 2022 maritime policy and law framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important system-level posture under Xi.

evidence.title: Joint Statement on the 20th Anniversary of the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea

evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for late-2022 regional diplomacy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Xi's state-led regional posture.

China continued coercive maritime behavior elsewhere in the same year.

evidence.title: Philippines slams Chinese coastguard’s 'close distance manoeuvring' at Scarborough Shoal

evidence.claim: The Philippine coast guard said a Chinese coast guard vessel maneuvered so closely that it constrained a Philippine patrol ship near Scarborough Shoal.

evidence.period_fit: Strong 2022 fit for South China Sea coercive behavior.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct as conduct by Chinese maritime forces under Xi's national-security authority.
contrary_evidence: China typically claims such actions are lawful enforcement in its own waters.

evidence.title: Indian, Chinese troops suffer minor injuries in clash on Dec 9: Indian army

contrary_evidence: The clash did not escalate into a wider war.
Both sides disengaged, and Chinese officials did not publicly escalate further.

evidence.title: OHCHR Assessment of human rights concerns in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, People's Republic of China

evidence.claim: OHCHR concluded that serious human rights violations were committed in Xinjiang under counter-terrorism and counter-extremism strategies, producing severe and undue restrictions and large-scale arbitrary deprivation of liberty with scant independent oversight.

evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 assessment of the Xinjiang policy environment relevant to Xi's domestic safety record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: Xi presided over the party-state that set the counter-terror framework and security posture.
contrary_evidence: The report does not assign personal criminal responsibility to Xi.
It focuses on the policy framework and documented pattern rather than individual orders.

evidence.title: China: Further information: Missing and arbitrarily detained in Xinjiang
evidence.claim: Amnesty said 48 additional people from predominantly Muslim ethnic groups had been interned or sentenced without a fair trial, bringing its campaign total to 120, and described the pattern as mass detention and torture affecting an estimated 1 million or more people since 2017.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material under Xi's leadership; the allegations concern the security system he controls.
contrary_evidence: This is advocacy reporting, not a court finding.
It uses estimated totals and campaign framing rather than a full official census.

evidence.title: China: Xi Jinping’s continued tenure as leader a disaster for human rights
evidence.claim: Amnesty said Xi's decade in power had featured sweeping arbitrary detentions, a nationwide crackdown on freedom of expression and association, crimes against humanity against Muslims in Xinjiang, and escalating repression in Hong Kong, with censorship tightened during politically sensitive periods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous Amnesty statement summarizing the 2022 rights environment under Xi.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for the 2022 political environment and Xi's third-term consolidation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the leadership level; it explicitly attributes the record to Xi's rule.
contrary_evidence: This is a rights-advocacy judgment, not a judicial verdict.
It compresses a decade-long pattern into a summary of 2022 conditions.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: China
evidence.claim: HRW reported that China imposed repeated, unpredictable lockdowns on hundreds of millions of people in 2022, in some cases using barriers to prevent people from leaving homes, and that people reported trouble accessing food and medical care, sometimes leading to deaths.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct in system-level terms: these were state policies under Xi's leadership, though carried out by local officials.
contrary_evidence: HRW is summarizing a national pattern and may understate local variation.
The page does not isolate Xi's personal orders from local implementation.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: China
evidence.claim: HRW said Hong Kong authorities under the Beijing-imposed security framework arrested people for national-security-related offenses, censored politically sensitive material, increased police surveillance, and constrained unions, universities, and media.

evidence.title: China: Government must not detain peaceful protesters as unprecedented demonstrations break out across the country
evidence.claim: Amnesty said the protests were peaceful, that authorities were likely to respond with censorship, surveillance, police force, and mass arrests, and that officials should not penalize people for protesting lockdown harms.

The statement includes predictive language about likely police actions as well as observed events.

evidence.title: Blank sheets of paper become symbol of defiance in China protests

It captures a narrow moment and does not quantify the full crackdown.

evidence.title: China set to loosen COVID curbs after week of historic protests
evidence.claim: Reuters said China was preparing to ease quarantine protocols and reduce mass testing after anger over the world's toughest curbs fueled widespread protests, with some cities already lifting lockdowns.

Policy easing did not end the broader repression pattern.

chapter_notes.RECON:
I used the local prior as the structured baseline and did not use the client matrix. I also kept this to a source-family summary, not an 80-lens score pass.

**What Xi’s office looked like in 2022**
- Xi held the core CCP/state posts: General Secretary of the CPC, Chairman of the CPC Central Military Commission, President of the PRC, and Chairman of the PRC Central Military Commission.
- The party constitution gives the General Secretary power to convene the Politburo and its Standing Committee and to preside over the Secretariat.
- The CMC chair has overall responsibility for the armed forces.
- In October 2022, the 20th Party Congress and its first plenary session renewed Xi as General Secretary and CMC chair, with a new Standing Committee packed with loyalists.

**What constrained him in 2022**
- The main constraints were practical and political, not formal checks.
- The zero-COVID system generated rare street and campus protests in late November.
- The government then moved quickly to soften quarantine/testing rules in early December.
- Economic headwinds were already present by mid-2022: mobility restrictions, weak normalization, and slowing growth.
- Rights criticism, especially around Xinjiang, Hong Kong, censorship, and protest suppression, remained intense.

**Best source families**
- Official Chinese party/state texts for office, authority, and policy position.
- Reuters for independent event chronology and external framing.
- SIPRI for security and military context.
- World Bank and IMF for macro conditions.
- Amnesty Chinese for critical local-language human-rights narrative.

**Retained Sources**
1. [Full text of Constitution of the Communist Party of China](https://english.court.gov.cn/2022-10/27/c_824962.htm) - Supreme People's Court / CPC Constitution text, 2022-10-27.  
   Precise fact: the General Secretary convenes the Politburo and Standing Committee and presides over the Secretariat; the CMC chair has overall responsibility for the armed forces.  
   Period fit: formal authority stack in late 2022.  
   Ruler attribution: direct, institutional.  
   Limitations: party legal text, not a behavioral record.  
   Contrary points: it does not show informal bargaining or implementation friction.

2. [Xi Jinping's report to the 20th National Congress of the CPC](https://www.xinhuanet.com/politics/leaders/2022-10/25/c_1129079429.htm) - Xinhua, 2022-10-25.  
   Precise fact: Xi’s report frames the congress around modernization, national rejuvenation, and strategic consolidation.  
   Period fit: captures Xi’s 2022 agenda and narrative frame.  
   Ruler attribution: direct, but from official propaganda.  
   Limitations: rhetorical and self-justifying, not an audit.  
   Contrary points: late-2022 protests and the policy reversal show that implementation was less stable than the report suggests.

3. [20th CPC Central Committee First Plenary Session Communique](https://www.xinhuanet.com/politics/cpc20/2022-10/23/c_1129075992.htm?id=488112) - Xinhua, 2022-10-23.  
   Precise fact: Xi was elected General Secretary and CMC chair; the new Standing Committee was filled with loyalists.  
   Period fit: immediate post-congress consolidation.  
   Ruler attribution: direct.  
   Limitations: official communiqué only, no dissent or process detail.  
   Contrary points: Reuters treats this as a precedent-breaking third term and notes the absence of a successor.

4. [China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/chinas-xi-clinches-third-term-packs-leadership-with-loyalists-2919033) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2022-10-23.  
   Precise fact: Xi secured a third leadership term and a loyalist top body.  
   Period fit: independent read on power consolidation in October 2022.  
   Ruler attribution: direct.  
   Limitations: wire framing, not a deep causal analysis.  
   Contrary points: official Chinese sources present the outcome as orderly party procedure and collective leadership.

5. [China tightens security after rare protests against COVID curbs](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-reports-another-daily-record-of-covid-cases-as-protests-ripple-across-china-2952419) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2022-11-27.  
   Precise fact: protests spread across cities and campuses; the dissent was unprecedented under Xi.  
   Period fit: major late-2022 constraint event.  
   Ruler attribution: indirect, but clearly a backlash against ruling policy.  
   Limitations: fast-moving protest reporting in a closed environment.  
   Contrary points: officials largely denied the unrest and framed controls as necessary public-health management.

6. [COVID-19 response further optimized with 10 new measures](https://english.www.gov.cn/statecouncil/ministries/202212/08/content_WS63913c92c6d0a757729e4135.html) - State Council / Xinhua, 2022-12-08.  
   Precise fact: the 10-point notice relaxed quarantine/testing and curbed arbitrary lockdown expansion.  
   Period fit: immediate post-protest policy shift.  
   Ruler attribution: direct state action under Xi’s system; personal attribution is inferential.  
   Limitations: official notice, no explicit causal link to protests.  
   Contrary points: it still described the move as optimization, not abandonment, of zero-COVID.

7. [World nuclear forces](https://www.sipri.org/yearbook/2023/07) - SIPRI Yearbook 2023, 2023.  
   Precise fact: China was in the middle of significant nuclear modernization and expansion; the stockpile was expected to keep growing.  
   Period fit: strategic baseline for 1B across 2022-2023.  
   Ruler attribution: indirect, state capability rather than personal conduct.  
   Limitations: open-source estimates, not Chinese official counts.  
   Contrary points: China’s declared no-first-use posture is not the same thing as stockpile growth.

8. [Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2022](https://www.sipri.org/publications/2023/sipri-fact-sheets/trends-world-military-expenditure-2022) - SIPRI, 2023-04-24.  
   Precise fact: China remained the world’s second-largest military spender in 2022, at roughly $292 billion.  
   Period fit: military burden and regional-security context for 2022.  
   Ruler attribution: indirect, state-level capacity.  
   Limitations: estimates, methodology and exchange-rate sensitivity.  
   Contrary points: spending level does not by itself prove aggressive intent or operational use.

9. [China Economic Update: Between Shocks and Stimulus](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099640106102210762) - World Bank, 2022-06-01.  
   Precise fact: Omicron outbreaks and mobility restrictions disrupted normalization and the World Bank projected sharper 2022 slowdown.  
   Period fit: inherited economic conditions before the late-2022 policy reversal.  
   Ruler attribution: indirect, macro conditions rather than personal conduct.  
   Limitations: forecast-oriented and technocratic.  
   Contrary points: official Chinese statistical releases can differ somewhat and later revisions can move the numbers.

10. [People's Republic of China: 2022 Article IV Consultation](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2023/067/002.2023.issue-067-en.xml) - IMF, 2023-02-03.  
   Precise fact: growth slowed significantly in 2022; policy turned expansionary; weak productivity and SOE structure clouded medium-term prospects.  
   Period fit: retrospective macro assessment of Xi’s 2022 environment.  
   Ruler attribution: indirect, policy environment rather than personal rule.  
   Limitations: macro and institution-focused, not a political narrative.  
   Contrary points: Chinese authorities emphasize stability, targeted stimulus, and long-run strategy.

11. [2022年度中国人权报告](https://www.amnesty.org/zh-hans/latest/research/2023/03/anuual-report-22-china/) - Amnesty International 中文, 2023-03-28.  
   Precise fact: documents harsh COVID restrictions, censorship, arrests of critics, and continued repression in Xinjiang, Tibet, and Hong Kong; it also ties the November protest wave to the Urumqi fire and lockdown anger.  
   Period fit: strong narrative summary of 2022 rights conditions.  
   Ruler attribution: direct to the Xi system, though not every act is personally ordered.  
   Limitations: advocacy-based and example-driven.  
   Contrary points: official Chinese claims frame the same policies as public-health necessity and national-security management.

**Compact event map**
- October 2022: 20th Party Congress, Xi secures a third term, and the new top leadership is stacked with loyalists.
- Late October 2022: the congress report and party constitution formalize the governing frame and the center’s authority.
- November 2022: rare protests erupt over COVID controls after the Urumqi fire.
- December 7-8, 2022: Beijing softens zero-COVID controls with 10 new measures.
- Mid-2022 through year-end: macro conditions remain weak, with slowed growth and policy strain.
- All year: repression and censorship remain central, with Xinjiang and Hong Kong still major external-pressure points.

- 7B: For corruption-specific work, add Transparency International and CCDI/party-discipline reporting; I did not retain those here because the cross-chapter set above was tighter.
- 8B: World Bank, IMF, State Council notices, and the Xinhua congress report.
